fatal_failures: production or authored tests do not compile and run from a clean offline copy
the caller-visible ComputeIntradayInterest operation is absent
the implementation uses no genuine generated CDM 7.0.0 object at its input or output boundary
elapsed interest is derived from calendar-date difference rather than the actual timestamp interval
equivalent cross-border timestamp representations can produce different amounts
a close-before-open input returns negative interest instead of failing
the main monetary calculation round-trips through double or float

criteria.description: Calculate the four-hour ACT/360 amount from actual elapsed seconds.
checks: USD 500,000,000 at 0.053 for 14,400 seconds produces exactly USD 12,268.52.
The implementation retains decimal precision through the formula and rounds only the final cash result to cents.
The output preserves USD and does not substitute a bare number for the monetary result.

criteria.description: Do not infer duration from dates or calendar boundaries.
checks: 22:00 UTC to 01:00 UTC the next day is exactly 10,800 seconds and produces the three-hour amount.
Crossing midnight does not create a full-day charge.
A same-date interval is not accidentally suppressed merely because its date difference is zero.

criteria.description: Make the result depend on instants rather than local wall-clock representation.
checks: One interval represented in Europe/London and Asia/Hong_Kong produces the same cent amount.
Offset or zone information is retained until the instants are established.
A daylight-saving transition is measured by actual elapsed seconds rather than apparent local hours.

criteria.description: Handle zero, sub-second, and reversed intervals deliberately.
checks: Equal timestamps and a positive duration shorter than one whole second return exact zero in the nominal currency.
A close even fractionally before open fails before whole-second truncation can disguise the reversal.
Null or malformed timestamps fail visibly and no path emits NaN, infinity, or negative elapsed interest.

criteria.description: Respect the selected basis and join continuously to ordinary one-day interest.
checks: A 24-hour interval equals nominal * rate / basis after the same final rounding policy.
ACT/360 and ACT/365 Fixed produce their distinct expected results.
Unsupported conventions fail closed instead of silently defaulting to 360 or 365.

criteria.description: Use a version-correct CDM boundary without pretending date-based generated behavior owns the intraday rule.
checks: The implementation uses coherent generated CDM 7.0.0 getters or builders for a timestamp, basis, nominal, rate, or monetary result boundary.
Any emitted CDM Money carries an exact value and currency unit and passes its structural plus applicable inherited data rules; another chosen CDM boundary is comparably defensible and validated.
DESIGN.md accurately labels elapsed-time normalisation and sub-day accrual as application behavior and does not claim a generated date day-count helper proves intraday semantics.

criteria.description: Deliver a stable, narrow implementation with meaningful tests and explicit numeric policy.
checks: Missing inputs, non-positive nominal, invalid or unsupported basis, and economically invalid rates are handled consistently with the documented contract.
Inputs and returned objects cannot be altered through application-owned mutable aliases, and the calculation has no current-clock, default-zone, or static-state dependency.
The five requested scenarios and close plausible-wrong controls pass from a clean offline Java 21/Gradle 8.10 copy.
